forces.title: Global payments revenue growth moderates, shifting competitive dynamics
forces.description: Global payments revenue growth is moderating from an average of 9 percent (2020-25) to a forecast 4 percent annually (2025-30). This structural shift necessitates a move from broad market momentum-driven growth to growth stemming from deliberate competitive advantages like operational discipline, pricing sophistication, and technological leadership, fundamentally altering value capture strategies.
forces.source_title: The 2026 Global Payments Report: Operational excellence in an invisible world

forces.title: Softening interest rate tailwinds impact net interest income in payments
forces.description: The elevated interest rate environment, which previously served as a strong cyclical tailwind driving rapid growth in net interest income (NII), is now softening. This dampens net interest margins and causes a projected shift in the global revenue mix, with NII's share decreasing from 46% in 2025 to 44% by 2030, making fee-based revenues more critical.
forces.source_title: The 2026 Global Payments Report: Operational excellence in an invisible world

forces.title: Generative AI and agentic commerce threaten deposit yields and card fees
forces.description: The rise of generative AI and agentic commerce poses a significant threat to traditional banking revenue pools. These autonomous software agents can optimize account yields, dynamically route transactions to minimize fees, and automate purchasing decisions, potentially squeezing deposit net interest income and consumer credit card fee pools by enabling balance migration and payment rail substitution. This could put $75 billion in global payments revenue at risk by 2030.
forces.source_title: The 2026 Global Payments Report: Operational excellence in an invisible world

forces.title: Payment infrastructure fragments into regional, multi-rail competitive arenas
forces.description: Contrary to theoretical predictions of network unification, payment infrastructure is fragmenting into regional, multi-rail competitive arenas. Institutions must navigate competing pressures from zero-fee domestic real-time account-to-account (A2A) networks, legacy card perimeters, and wholesale stablecoin corridors for cross-border settlement. This fragmentation creates complex strategic boundaries and operational challenges for financial service providers.
forces.source_title: The 2026 Global Payments Report: Operational excellence in an invisible world

forces.title: Digital assets bypass traditional economics, creating revenue headwinds for payments
forces.description: Digital assets like stablecoins and tokenized deposits are posing an additional headwind to traditional payments and deposit revenues. They bypass traditional interchange fees and foreign-exchange (FX) conversion markups, and shift float income out of commercial bank deposits. As cross-border corporate corridors adopt tokenized settlement, providers will face direct margin pressure on FX spreads and correspondent banking fees.
forces.source_title: The 2026 Global Payments Report: Operational excellence in an invisible world

forces.title: Weaker mortgage lending and higher rates constrain Belgian housing market
forces.description: The Belgian housing market faces significant headwinds from persistently weaker mortgage lending and higher long-term interest rates. Despite some resilience in Q2 2026, the number of new mortgages in the first eight months of the year remained 10% below the previous year. These restrictive financing conditions are expected to lead to a cooling market with modest house price increases in the coming years.
forces.source_title: Second-quarter resilience masks a more challenging outlook for Belgian housing

forces.title: Intensifying competition from nonbank financial institutions for client wallet share
forces.description: Nonbank financial institutions, including fintechs, private credit firms, direct institutional lenders, and nonbank market makers (NBMMs), are increasingly competing for client wallet share across corporate, institutional investor, and financial sponsor segments. Approximately 40% of corporates are open to nonbank financing in the next three years, with NBMMs capturing 9-14% of wallet share by asset class, indicating significant wallet leakage from traditional banks.
forces.source_title: Anchor or drift: What it takes to capture wallet share in 2026

forces.title: Customer primacy and deposits shift to neobanks and fintechs
forces.description: Neobanks and fintechs now hold approximately 27 percent of all UK banking relationships, a significant increase from a decade ago. This shift in customer primacy means incumbents risk losing their stable and inexpensive deposit bases. AI agents are expected to accelerate this trend by making it easier for customers to switch products and move money, further challenging traditional banking relationships and funding models.
forces.source_title: The decade to redefine UK banking

forces.title: AI accelerating unbundling and disintermediation in banking services
forces.description: AI's rapid and broad adoption, significantly faster than previous technologies, is removing historical frictions in banking processes like onboarding, KYC, and product switching. Agentic AI can continuously compare rates and automatically move idle balances, potentially causing deposit profits to fall by 20% or more if 5-10% of balances migrate. This drives disintermediation, with AI directing consumers to digital-native lenders.
forces.source_title: The decade to redefine UK banking

forces.title: New high-growth arenas create demand for innovative insurance solutions
forces.description: Eighteen identified 'arenas' like AI software, electrification, and bio-frontiers are generating new asset categories, technologies, liabilities, and behaviors that reshape risk exposures. This creates substantial new demand for insurance, requiring new product offerings, distribution models, and underwriting capabilities. These arenas present opportunities for insurers to access new premium pools and build differentiated capabilities, despite the novel risks involved.
forces.source_title: The strategic new arenas reshaping insurance

forces.title: Slowdown in premium growth impacts traditional insurance lines
forces.description: The insurance industry, particularly Property & Casualty (P&C), is entering a more moderate growth phase. After a period of strong premium expansion driven by rate increases, the slowdown in rate growth over the past 12 months has resulted in overall premium growth deceleration and limited expansion of underlying coverage in many markets. This necessitates insurers to seek profitable growth beyond traditional and mature risk pools.
forces.source_title: The strategic new arenas reshaping insurance

forces.title: Climate change, cyber threats, and geopolitics raise insurance loss uncertainty
forces.description: Global risk pools are being reshaped by climate change, cyber threats, and geopolitical volatility, leading to increased loss uncertainty and correlation across risks. Global insured losses from natural catastrophes exceeded $127 billion in 2025. These interconnected and rapidly evolving risks, often with limited historical loss experience, challenge existing underwriting models and require innovative risk-sharing and capital structures.
forces.source_title: The strategic new arenas reshaping insurance

forces.title: Arena risks shift to less frequent but higher-severity insurance events
forces.description: New 'arena' risks, driven by technological innovations, tend towards less frequent but far higher-severity events. For instance, technology in auto claims reduces frequency but increases severity. This change demands insurers to adapt their risk assessment and reserving, moving from models optimized for high-frequency, low-severity events to those that can handle rare but catastrophically expensive occurrences with potentially new correlations across different lines of business.
forces.source_title: The strategic new arenas reshaping insurance

forces.title: GLP-1 obesity drugs and bio-frontiers transform life insurance mortality assumptions
forces.description: Bio-frontiers, specifically GLP-1 obesity drugs, genetic modification, and personalized medicine, are set to transform life and annuities by shifting underlying mortality and morbidity pricing assumptions. GLP-1 drugs could lead to significant mortality improvement, systematically overpricing treated populations with outdated models. Genomics moves towards highly individualized risk profiles, fundamentally altering how life risk is segmented and raising ethical/regulatory questions.
forces.source_title: The strategic new arenas reshaping insurance

forces.title: Electric vehicle adoption drives higher claims severity and costs in auto insurance
forces.description: The adoption of Electric Vehicles (EVs) is propelling higher claims severity in auto insurance. Battery damage frequently leads to total-loss write-offs, and repairs cost 20-30% more than internal combustion engine equivalents. Thermal runaway introduces a fire propagation risk that crosses into property lines (e.g., home garages). Insurers face compounding exposure: fewer claims but significantly higher per-claim costs and new correlations between auto and homeowner books.
forces.source_title: The strategic new arenas reshaping insurance

forces.title: Shared autonomous vehicles shift auto risk to system failures and platform liability
forces.description: As shared autonomous vehicles (AVs) deploy, risk shifts from frequent, uncorrelated human error claims to less frequent but higher-severity, correlated system risks (software defects, outages, cyberattacks). Liability fundamentally shifts from individual drivers to platforms, OEMs, and technology providers, reshaping personal auto policies and increasing the need for commercial fleet and liability coverage based on system performance and operational data.
forces.source_title: The strategic new arenas reshaping insurance

forces.title: Cybersecurity for commercial lines amplifies systemic correlation risks
forces.description: Cyber risk has evolved into dynamic threat environments amplified by AI-enabled attacks. For commercial insurance, the fundamental challenge is systemic correlation: a single vulnerability in widely deployed software can trigger simultaneous claims across thousands of policyholders, akin to a natural catastrophe. This means portfolio diversification offers less protection, and tail correlations exceed traditional reinsurance capacity, necessitating new capital structures and advanced analytics.
forces.source_title: The strategic new arenas reshaping insurance

forces.title: Cloud services create business interruption correlation risks for insurers
forces.description: The widespread reliance on cloud services creates significant correlation issues for business interruption claims. A single outage from a major cloud provider can trigger losses across thousands of dependent businesses simultaneously, violating the independence assumption of standard property underwriting. This cascades across multiple tenants, operators, and programs, posing a systemic risk to commercial insurers that requires re-evaluation of coverage models.
forces.source_title: The strategic new arenas reshaping insurance

forces.title: Robotics create new liability risks and ambiguous fault attribution in insurance
forces.description: As autonomous robots expand beyond factories into public spaces, they create new liability potential and situations where fault attribution becomes ambiguous. Software failures, fleet interconnections, and AI decision-making make it harder to establish causation than with traditional machinery. Claims are shifting from workers' compensation to product liability, requiring fundamentally different underwriting approaches and new dedicated coverage for humanoid and embodied-AI robots.
forces.source_title: The strategic new arenas reshaping insurance

forces.title: Regulated AI models demand explainability and continuous validation for financial decisions
forces.description: Financial regulators, such as the Bank of England's Prudential Regulation Authority, expect AI models used in regulated decisions (e.g., credit risk, KYC checks) to remain fully explainable, traceable, and subject to continuous validation. While AI offers productivity gains, banks moving fast to implement agentic workflows must concurrently stay on top of governance and monitoring issues, acting as a constraint and risk factor for rapid AI adoption.
forces.source_title: The decade to redefine UK banking

viewpoints.title: Global payments growth moderates, shifting focus to operational excellence and competitive advantages
viewpoints.description: McKinsey states that global payments revenue growth is moderating from 9 percent to 4 percent annually, signaling a structural transition. This shift means future growth will depend less on broad market momentum and more on deliberate competitive advantages such as commercial excellence, operational discipline, and technological leadership. This necessitates a strategic re-evaluation for payments providers to ensure value capture.
viewpoints.source_title: The 2026 Global Payments Report: Operational excellence in an invisible world

viewpoints.title: EMEA payments market faces margin compression and slow growth from lower interest rates
viewpoints.description: McKinsey identifies that the Europe, Middle East, and Africa (EMEA) region is experiencing margin compression due to lower interest rates, which are impacting treasury and deposit margins. This is prompting a rapid shift to fee-based structures. Growth is projected to slow to approximately 3 percent annually in 2025–30, a sharp decline from the 14 percent annual growth observed in 2020–25.
viewpoints.source_title: The 2026 Global Payments Report: Operational excellence in an invisible world

viewpoints.title: Belgian housing market outlook challenging due to weak mortgage lending and high interest rates
viewpoints.description: ING Think reports that while the Belgian housing market showed unexpected resilience in Q2 2026, the underlying trend of weaker mortgage production and sustained higher interest rates points to a loss of momentum. The outlook remains challenging, with nominal median house prices expected to increase by a modest 2.5% in 2026 and 2.0% in 2027, following a period of real price declines.
viewpoints.source_title: Second-quarter resilience masks a more challenging outlook for Belgian housing

viewpoints.title: Financial institutions must address agentic commerce infrastructure proactively, despite adoption uncertainties
viewpoints.description: McKinsey advises that financial institutions and payment operators cannot delay in addressing agentic commerce, even if widespread consumer adoption is years away. The critical infrastructure battle—establishing how machines authenticate, consent, and route transactions—is occurring now. Proactive engagement in building the trust layer is essential for competitive positioning and value capture in the evolving payments landscape.
viewpoints.source_title: The 2026 Global Payments Report: Operational excellence in an invisible world

viewpoints.title: Banking relationships no longer guaranteed, requiring continuous effort to retain wallet share
viewpoints.description: McKinsey’s survey indicates that banking relationships are no longer evergreen, with clients (corporates, institutional investors, financial sponsors) continuously optimizing their provider ecosystems. This leads to 12% to 25% of annual banking wallet share being reallocated. Banks must treat loyalty as earned annually, focusing on performance, service, and delivery, rather than assuming client relationships are secure.
viewpoints.source_title: Anchor or drift: What it takes to capture wallet share in 2026

viewpoints.title: UK banking profitability masks eroding foundations amid competition and AI disruption
viewpoints.description: McKinsey highlights that despite UK banks enjoying high returns on tangible equity, their underlying profit foundations are eroding. This is driven by customer primacy shifting to neobanks and fintechs, intensifying commercial banking competition, and AI accelerating disintermediation. The grace period for incumbents is closing rapidly, demanding strategic responses to secure customers, transactions, and rebuild cost structures with AI.
viewpoints.source_title: The decade to redefine UK banking

viewpoints.title: Incumbent banks can reclaim wallet share by matching challengers and leveraging their edge
viewpoints.description: McKinsey suggests incumbent banks can reclaim contestable wallet share by adapting to new competitive dynamics. This involves matching fintechs on digital experience, private credit firms on speed and flexibility, and nonbank market makers on execution. By doing so, banks can leverage their existing advantages such as regulatory robustness, breadth of product, and relationship continuity, where challengers currently fall short.
viewpoints.source_title: Anchor or drift: What it takes to capture wallet share in 2026

viewpoints.title: UK neobanks have evolved into scaled, profitable competitors challenging incumbents' core businesses
viewpoints.description: McKinsey notes that leading UK neobanks have crossed the threshold from niche challengers to scaled, profitable competitors, demonstrating that digital-first models can effectively acquire customers and deposits. This evolution is evidenced by entities like Revolut securing a full UK banking license and expanding into traditional profit pools such as mortgages and private banking, directly pressuring incumbents.
viewpoints.source_title: The decade to redefine UK banking

viewpoints.title: Banks' grace period for AI adoption is rapidly closing, demanding swift strategic responses
viewpoints.description: McKinsey emphasizes that AI adoption is occurring much faster and more broadly than previous technology waves, drastically lowering friction for financial tasks. This acceleration means the historical grace period for banks to adopt new technologies is closing. Incumbents face disintermediation risks, particularly in deposit profits, underscoring the critical need for rapid AI implementation to maintain competitive relevance.
viewpoints.source_title: The decade to redefine UK banking

viewpoints.title: Incumbent banks can leverage trust and data to transform AI into a competitive advantage
viewpoints.description: McKinsey argues that incumbents possess strong advantages including large tech budgets, extensive proprietary data, established customer relationships, and regulatory experience. These assets, combined with customer trust (64% of UK AI users trust their primary bank most for AI services), offer a crucial opportunity. Banks that move swiftly to build on this trust can effectively turn AI from a disruptive threat into their sharpest competitive tool.
viewpoints.source_title: The decade to redefine UK banking

viewpoints.title: Eighteen high-growth industries offer a new wave of demand and disruption for insurance
viewpoints.description: McKinsey identifies 18 'arenas' across themes like AI foundation, digitization, electrification, hard tech, and new bio-frontiers. These arenas are reshaping risk exposures across the economy, creating new asset categories, technologies, and liabilities. This fundamental shift generates significant new demand for insurance products and distribution models, presenting a major growth opportunity for the sector.
viewpoints.source_title: The strategic new arenas reshaping insurance

viewpoints.title: Insurers face moderate growth, spurring search for value beyond traditional lines
viewpoints.description: McKinsey reports that insurers, particularly in P&C, are entering a phase of moderate premium growth after a period of strong expansion driven largely by rate increases. As rate growth slows, carriers are seeking new sources of profitable growth beyond mature risk pools and traditional lines. This context makes the identified high-growth 'arenas' crucial for future value creation, despite their novel and complex risks.
viewpoints.source_title: The strategic new arenas reshaping insurance

demand_drivers.description: Payment transaction value grew roughly 1.2 times faster than nominal global GDP from 2020 to 2025.
Providers increased revenue per transaction by embedding software, fraud mitigation, and data services into the transaction flow.

pnl_drivers.description: Elevated interest rate environment drove rapid growth in net interest income (NII). Fading tailwinds lead to NII share decreasing from 46% (2025) to 44% (2030), while fee income rises from 54% to 56%.

market_sizing.methodology: Global payments revenue. Generated from 3.8 trillion transactions and $2.1 quadrillion in annual value flows. Represents roughly 41 percent of total banking revenues. Growth moderating from 9% (2020-25 average) to 4% (2025-30 forecast).
market_sizing.source_title: The 2026 Global Payments Report: Operational excellence in an invisible world

pnl_drivers.description: Software agents automatically sweep idle cash to higher-yielding accounts and investment products, causing balance migration and yield compression (estimated $65 billion at risk).
Through payment rail substitution, automated repayment optimization, fee avoidance, and real-time foreign-exchange routing (estimated $10 billion at risk).

market_sizing.methodology: Global payments revenue at risk from agentic AI under a baseline adoption scenario. This is equivalent to 4 percent of the $1.9 trillion pool of retail and commercial deposits and consumer credit card revenues.
market_sizing.source_title: The 2026 Global Payments Report: Operational excellence in an invisible world

pnl_drivers.description: Post-2008 reform gives UK banks a stable and inexpensive deposit base.
Concentration in balance sheet terms protects spread income despite intensifying competition.
Higher lending margins due to rising interest rates (net interest margin rose six basis points between 2024 and 2025).

market_sizing.methodology: Total UK banking revenue after risk costs (net of loan-loss provisions) for retail and commercial segments. Retail banking generated approximately £62 billion, and commercial banking £32 billion.
market_sizing.source_title: The decade to redefine UK banking

demand_drivers.description: Agentic AI is expected to increasingly move idle retail balances into higher-yield products, as well as corporate treasurers shifting cash into tokenised treasury products.
Britain has a chronic advice gap, with only ~9% of adults receiving regulated advice last year, compared to ~33% in the United States, creating an opportunity for wealth managers.

new_opportunities.description: Banks can convert deposits into assets under management, leveraging wealth as the fastest-growing retail pool at around 7% annually.
new_opportunities.opportunity: Convert deposit outflows into wealth inflows

market_sizing.methodology: Estimated range for mass and affluent savings that could migrate from deposits into investments in the UK over the next decade. This is part of a larger UK cash pile exceeding £2 trillion.
market_sizing.source_title: The decade to redefine UK banking
